content: this method is pub(crate) now, but I need to get raw nanoseconds out of clock code in a driver.

I think it's fine, but it would be better to rename the function to something like as_ktime(). What the returned value means depends on the clock. So the name should simply say that it returns the C ktime_t value.

Which clock do you use?
the current C driver just does ktime_to_ns(ktime_get()) so I think I just want Instant::<Monotonic>::now().as_nanos() to work
I think we can just make it public
No objection to making it public. Not a strong opinion, but since we have Instant::from_ktime(), renaming it to as_ktime() would make a more logical pair.
I mean, if what Dave wants is nanoseconds, then calling a method called as_nanos() seems like the way to go.
Fair enough, though what as_nanos() represents depends on the clock.
Yes, ktime_t is always in nanoseconds. Only the starting point depends on the clock.
